historical_references.reference: Adbhutansh was a celebrated poet and scholar in the royal court of the Gupta king Harshavardhana (606-647 AD). He was a master of Sanskrit and composed several works of poetry and prose. In particular, he wrote a Sanskrit commentary on the Bhagavad Gita, the sacred text of Hinduism, which is still studied and revered today.

Adbhutansh also wrote a commentary on the Mahabharata, the great Indian epic, that was highly regarded in medieval India. His commentary, known as the 'Bharata-tattva', was particularly noted for its clarity and depth of interpretation. Adbhutansh's works were an important contribution to the rich literary tradition of Hinduism during the medieval period.
